description_full: EDP Renewables, S.A. engages in the renewable energy business in Europe, North America, South America, and the Asia Pacific. The company is involved in the planning, construction, operation, and maintenance of power generation plants using renewable energy sources, including wind and solar power. It operates in Spain, Portugal, Belgium, France, Italy, Germany, the Netherlands, Poland, Romania, the United Kingdom, Hungary, Greece, the United States, Canada, Mexico, Brazil, Chile, South Korea, Singapore, Vietnam, Thailand, China, Taiwan, Australia, and Japan. EDP Renewables, S.A. was formerly known as EDP Renováveis, S.A. and changed its name to EDP Renewables, S.A. in April 2026. The company was incorporated in 2007 and is headquartered in Madrid, Spain. EDP Renewables, S.A. operates as a subsidiary of EDP, S.A.

financial_summary: EDP Renovaveis SA is a large-cap utilities business with a $14.3B market cap on $3.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +7% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 3% against a 6% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 80% confirm genuine pricing power.
The company is burning through $2.0B of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 10.1× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 2.3× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.3%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 71% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
